subject: physiology
title: Gastric acid secretion, parietal cell physiology and regulatory peptides
refs: Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology

steps.tx: Gastric **parietal cells** in the oxyntic glands of the gastric corpus and fundus secrete hydrochloric acid and intrinsic factor. Hydrochloric acid reduces luminal pH to approximately one point five, sterilizing ingested food, denaturing proteins and activating pepsinogen into proteolytic pepsin. Intrinsic factor is a glycoprotein essential for terminal ileal absorption of cobalamin, deficiency of which produces megaloblastic pernicious anemia and subacute combined degeneration.
steps.say: Gastric parietal cells in the oxyntic glands secrete hydrochloric acid and intrinsic factor. Hydrochloric acid reduces luminal pH to one point five, sterilizing ingested food, denaturing proteins and activating pepsinogen into pepsin. Intrinsic factor is a glycoprotein essential for terminal ileal absorption of cobalamin, preventing pernicious anemia.

steps.tx: The molecular engine of acid secretion is the apical **proton pump** or hydrogen-potassium ATPase. Carbonic anhydrase hydrates carbon dioxide into carbonic acid, which dissociates into protons and bicarbonate. Basolateral chloride-bicarbonate exchangers export bicarbonate into blood, creating the postprandial alkaline tide, while importing chloride. Apical hydrogen-potassium ATPase pumps protons into the lumen in exchange for potassium, accompanied by chloride efflux.
steps.say: The molecular engine of acid secretion is the apical proton pump or hydrogen-potassium ATPase. Carbonic anhydrase hydrates carbon dioxide into carbonic acid, yielding protons and bicarbonate. Basolateral exchangers export bicarbonate into blood, creating the alkaline tide, while importing chloride. The proton pump secretes protons in exchange for potassium.

vis.alt: Parietal cell: carbonic anhydrase makes hydrogen and bicarbonate, the apical H+ K+ ATPase pumps hydrogen into the lumen for potassium, K+ and Cl- channels supply the ions, a basolateral Cl- HCO3- exchanger sends bicarbonate to blood (alkaline tide); acetylcholine, gastrin and histamine stimulate and proton pump inhibitors block the pump.
vis.caption: Histamine, gastrin and acetylcholine all converge on the proton pump; omeprazole blocks the pump itself.

steps.tx: Three physiological agonists stimulate parietal cell acid secretion through distinct intracellular pathways. **Histamine** from enterochromaffin-like cells binds H2 receptors, activating adenylyl cyclase and cyclic AMP. **Acetylcholine** from vagal postganglionic terminals binds M3 receptors, and **gastrin** from G cells binds CCK-B receptors, both activating phospholipase C and inositol trisphosphate. Proton pump inhibitors covalently bind and irreversibly block the final common pathway.
steps.say: Three physiological agonists stimulate parietal cell acid secretion. Histamine from enterochromaffin-like cells binds H2 receptors, raising cyclic AMP. Acetylcholine from vagus nerve binds M3 receptors, and gastrin from G cells binds CCK-B receptors, both raising intracellular calcium. Proton pump inhibitors irreversibly block the hydrogen-potassium ATPase pump.

points: Potentiate one another for maximal secretory response

right.title: Acid inhibitors
points: Somatostatin via paracrine SST2 receptor (lowers cAMP)
Prostaglandin E2 via EP3 receptor (protects mucosa)
Secretin released by duodenal S cells upon acidification
Negative feedback triggered when antral pH falls below 3

steps.tx: The peptide hormone **somatostatin** is the master paracrine inhibitor of gastric secretion. Released by antral D cells when luminal pH falls below three, somatostatin binds Gi-coupled receptors on G cells and enterochromaffin-like cells, suppressing gastrin and histamine release directly. Prostaglandin E2 similarly stimulates mucosal mucus and bicarbonate barrier secretion while decreasing parietal cyclic AMP. Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs inhibit prostaglandin synthesis, causing peptic ulceration.
